In 2022, Apple made history when its film "CODA" won the Academy Award for Best Picture. Now, the release date for the new film from that movie's director, "Being Heumann," has been confirmed on Apple TV+.

"Being Heumann," directed by the filmmaker behind "CODA," will debut on Apple TV+ this November.

Apple's film division has had its ups and downs, and the success of "CODA" is undoubtedly one of the finest examples of the former.

"CODA" won Best Picture at the 2022 Academy Awards, along with two other major prizes. With this achievement, Apple TV+ became the first streaming platform in history to win the Oscars' top film honour.

The next project from "CODA" director Sian Heder is also set to arrive soon, likewise distributed by Apple.

"Being Heumann" will have an early theatrical release in select cinemas on November 6, before officially launching on Apple TV+ on November 13.

"Entertainment Weekly" exclusively revealed several stills from the new film today, alongside multiple interview excerpts with Heder about the project.

"Being Heumann" and the previously announced "Tenzing" are both considered strong contenders for Apple original films eyeing next year's Academy Awards.

These two works will complement a slate of new Apple films aimed at general audiences, including the pickleball-themed comedy "The Dink," which opens this week.

What do you think of Apple's upcoming film lineup? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.

Apple TV+ is priced at US$12.99 per month, with discounts available when subscribing through the Apple One bundle.
